title: EU traffic fencing + tiered fallback safeguards
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Objective: implement a tenant-scoped traffic-fencing mechanism that guarantees EU-only handling for tenants which require data residency, while providing a controlled, auditable tiered fallback path when EU capacity or compatible model variants are temporarily unavailable. Scope: evaluation and enforcement of tenant allowlists/denylists, per-tenant residency flags, routing precedence across region/tier/model-variant, and an emergency escape policy. Non-goals: model training, long-term storage retention policy changes, or billing model redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Tenants with 'eu_only' flag are never routed to non-EU regions except when emergency_fallback is active and explicitly allowed by policy
Policy evaluator supports tenant-level allowlist and denylist entries and returns an auditable decision object for every request
Fallback chain implemented: primary EU-compatible variant -> EU-compatible lower-tier variant -> controlled cross-region failover with audit+notify
End-to-end tests cover normal, degraded (EU saturated), and emergency (EU outage) scenarios with expected routing outcomes
Console shows per-tenant routing decisions and exposes a toggle for emergency_fallback with role-restricted access
implementation_notes: Add a Policy Decision Service (PDS) hook in the routing path that returns: {decision, reason_code, matched_rules, trace_id} as a flat stringified JSON in logs
Precedence: tenant denylist > tenant allowlist > account residency flag > region affinity > default routing. Documented and unit-tested order in control plane
Model variant registry will include metadata: compatible_regions (list), tier (e.g., premium/standard/compat), memory_profile, and fallback_score

Routing algorithm: evaluate PDS -> select compatible variants in same-region same-tier sorted by fallback_score -> if none, consider same-region lower-tier -> if none and emergency_fallback enabled, allow cross-region with telemetry and customer notification
Implement soft-circuit-breaker: when EU latencies or error rates exceed thresholds, PDS can mark region 'degraded' for X seconds to trigger fallback evaluation
Enforcement split: decision made in control plane, enforcement at edge routers. Use signed policy tokens to avoid TOCTOU issues when routing handoff occurs
Persist routing decision and minimal request fingerprint in audit log (tenant_id, decision, reason_code, model_variant, region, timestamp, trace_id) for 90 days by default
Expose per-tenant config in Console under 'Data Residency' with role-based controls and an audit trail
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Lab: local integration tests with simulated EU saturation (done)
Phase 2 - Canary: enable routing for 5 non-sensitive tenants, monitor routing decisions and latency/ERROR budget for 48h
Phase 3 - Gradual: expand to 25% of EU-only tenants with automated rollback on alert thresholds
Phase 4 - Enforced: flip 'eu_only' enforcement for all tenants after 2 weeks of stable metrics and security sign-off
Feature flags: pds_routing_v2, emergency_fallback_toggle, audit_enforcement; default to disabled in production until Phase 3
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: percentage of requests honoring tenant residency (goal 100%)
Metric: count of fallback-to-cross-region events per hour (alert > 5 for > 10m)
SLO: <=1% unauthorized cross-region routing per quarter; alert and auto-rollback if breached
Log: structured audit event for every routing decision (exportable to compliance dashboard)
Dashboards: per-tenant decision rate, error/latency in EU region, and fallback chain distribution
